description.narrative: The proposed The AF comprises funding from a GEF/LDCF grant of US$8.05 million and a PROGREEN grant of US$4.50 million. This funding will scale up interventions under the RESILAND Mali Landscape Restoration Project (P177041), as well as introduce complementary activities. The project will retain its existing component structure, with the Additional Financing integrated within Components 1, 2, and 3. The institutional arrangements will remain entirely unchanged: the same implementation framework, coordination mechanisms, fiduciary responsibilities, and reporting lines will continue to apply without any modification. This ensures continuity in implementation, preserves established roles and responsibilities across all institutions involved, and maintains the efficiency and coherence of project management under the existing setup.Components The AF activities that will scale up interventions under the parent project and introduce complementary activities include:Component 1: Institutional Support and Capacity Building for Landscape Restoration and Climate Resilience (LCDF US$ 2.40m and PROGREEN US$ 1.40m). The AF will scale up institutional and technical capacity building activities under Sub-component 1.1. and Sub-component 1.2. Under Sub-component 1.1.1: Capacity Development, the AF will scale up academic and professional training through the expansion of the master's Program in Sustainable Development Engineering and Environmental Management, including training at least 70 new participants to strengthen national expertise in sustainable land management, climate change, and environmental governance. Under Sub-component 1.1.2: Enabling Environment for Mobilizing Climate Finance, the AF will scale up support to strengthen forest monitoring and management capacities through AI-based forest inventory systems, training of cartographers, pilot testing of digital forest monitoring with field verification, procurement of drones and forest surveillance equipment, and training of forest stakeholders on legal and regulatory frameworks related to forest management and resilience, targeting 400 participants, including 45 percent women. The AF will also finance new activities including (i) training and capacity building to strengthen institutional coordination, implementation oversight, and technical leadership within the Agency for Environment and Sustainable Development (AEDD); and (ii) installation of solar energy systems for selected Regional Directorates of Water and Forests and key structures of the Ministry of Environment, Sanitation and Sustainable Development (MEADD). These investments will reduce dependence on increasingly unstable energy supply, improve coordination and communication between local, regional, and national MEADD structures, and support the continuous delivery and monitoring of core environmental and climate related functions.Under Sub-component 1.2.2: Updating and Developing Forest and Pastoral Management Plans, the AF will finance the implementation of restoration, rehabilitation, and related activities under at least three forest management plans developed under the parent project and in several urban green spaces. Component 2: Investments in Landscape Restoration and Community Resilience to Climate Impacts (LCDF US$ 5.35m and PROGREEN US$ 3.00m). The AF will scale up interventions under Sub-component 2.1 Restoring Landscapes and Ecosystem Services and Sub-component 2.2 Improving Local Livelihoods Resilience. In addition, under a new sub-component, Sub-component 2.2.4 Climate Adaptation and Clean Energy Solutions activity, the AF will finance three productive alliance subprojects focused on: (i) production and dissemination of green charcoal, (ii) promotion and scaling up of solar cooking solutions, and (iii) development and adoption of alternative fuel briquettes. Under Sub-component 2.1: Restoring Landscapes and Ecosystem Services, the AF will scale up efforts in agroforestry systems, assisted natural regeneration, climate-resilient plantations, soil and water conservation measures, and restoration of degraded ecosystems, including vegetation cover, pastoral areas, nurseries, and small water bodies through the at least 15 additional restoration and SLM sub-projects. It will also support the implementation of priority activities under approved forest management plans, including reforestation, enrichment planting, forest protection, and community-based forest governance.Under Sub-component 2.2: Improving Local Livelihoods Resilience, the Additional Financing (AF) will scale up activities as follows: The Additional Financing will deepen support to livelihoods linked to restored landscapes by strengthening value chains and productive partnerships that translate restoration outcomes into sustained economic opportunities. Support will be provided for the development and financing of productive alliances and business plans in non-timber forest products (NTFPs) and fisheries, with the objective of strengthening linkages between producers, processors, and markets and improving the commercial viability of nature-based activities. The AF will also scale up integrated agro sylvo pastoral farms (FACI), combining forestry, livestock, cropping, fisheries, market gardening, apiculture, and small livestock to promote diversified, climate resilient livelihood systems.• Sub-component 2.2.1: Community integrated agro-sylvo-pastoral farms (FACI). The AF will support the establishment of two (2) additional FACIs, complementing the twenty (20) FACIs already planned under the parent project. • Sub-component 2.2.2: Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) value chains. The AF will finance two (2) additional productive alliances in the NTFP sector, supporting the development of at least ten (10) business plans. • Sub-component 2.2.3: Community fisheries and aquaculture systems. The AF will support one (1) additional productive alliance in the fisheries sector, with the implementation of at least twenty (20) business plans. For productive alliances in the fisheries and NTFP sectors, the AF will complement the one hundred (100) business plans initially planned under the parent project by financing at least thirty (30) additional business plans.In addition, under a new additional Sub-component 2.2.6, the Additional Financing (AF) will expand the scope of interventions through a new activity on Climate Adaptation and Clean Energy Solutions, by supporting three productive alliance subprojects centred on clean and climate-resilient energy pathways. These will target: (i) sustainable green charcoal value chains, (ii) the deployment of solar-based cooking solutions, and (iii) the development of alternative biomass briquettes from agricultural and organic residues. Together, these investments are designed to ease pressure on forest ecosystems while advancing a more sustainable, inclusive, and resilient energy transition. This sub-component will follow the same implementation arrangements as the SC2.2.2 and SC2.2.3 productive alliances through matching grants to local producers.Component 3: Coordination, Monitoring and Evaluation (LCDF US$ 0.30m and PROGREEN US$ 0.10m. The AF will provide enhanced support to project coordination, as well as to monitoring and evaluation functions, to ensure effective oversight and the successful implementation of AF activities.
To increase adoption of climate smart landscape restoration practices and access to income earning opportunities

condition.narrative: ESS 10.2 of the ESCP: No later than 3 months after the Effective Date, the PMU shall establish the project Grievance Mechanism andthereafter maintain it operational throughout the implementation of the Project.
No later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, the PMU shall recruit an external auditor to audit annual financialstatements.
No later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, the PMU shall install an accounting software for the project.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.4(a) of the Financing Agreement: No later than three (3) months after the Effective Date or such later dateas agreed by the Association, the PMU shall recruit and thereafter maintain an accountant, an assistant accountant, an internalauditor, an M&E specialist, an environmental safeguard specialist, a social safeguard specialist and a gender-based violencespecialist; with adequate experience, qualification and terms of reference acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.5(a) of the Financing Agreement: No later than three months after the Effective Date, or such later date asagreed by the Association, the Recipient shall establish, and thereafter maintain the Regional Support Units (RSUs) in each regionof the Recipient targeted under the Project, in form and manner and with terms of reference and resources acceptable to theAssociation.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.6 of the Financing Agreement: No later than three months after the Effective Date, or such later date asagreed by the Association, the Recipient shall hire a technical assistance firm satisfactory to the Association for the provisionof support to the PMU in areas related to, inter alia¸ landscape restoration topics, procurement, technical, fiduciary, andenvironmental and social risk activities, including support to the design and implementation of a participatory and inclusivemonitoring and evaluation system, communication and knowledge sharing, preparation of terms of reference for consultants forsafeguard instruments or technical activities, and Project reporting, all in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement andas further set out in the PIM.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.7(a) of the Financing Agreement: No later than three months after the Effective Date, or such later date asagreed by the Association, the Recipient shall hire partner institutions satisfactory to the Association for the provision oftechnical support to the PMU and RSUs for the preparation and implementation of Subprojects in close collaboration with theRecipient's deconcentrated technical services, civil society organizations, private sector, and commune representatives includingthe land commissions, religious and customary authorities, and to carry out such other tasks as may be defined from time to time inthe PIM, all in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement and as further set out in the PIM.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.8(a) of the Financing Agreement: No later than three months after the Effective Date, or such later date asagreed by the Association, the Recipient shall ensure that the PMU enters into various Cooperation Agreements with the differentnational institutions (“Project Entities”) involved in the implementation of different Project activities, all in form andsubstance satisfactory to the Association, and as further set out in the PIM.

title.narrative: Terrestrial and aquatic areas under enhanced conservation and management

comment.narrative:
To date, 14,738 hectares are under SLM through the implementation of 118 sub-projects. The implementation of the 5 Development and Management Plans (PAG) for massifs and classified forests covering 12,681 hectares as well as 5 pastoral units covering a total area of 1,800 hectares are planned. The implementation of these activities are expected to increase the land area under SLM to approximately 80,000 hectares for a total of 90,000 hectares.
The value for the period is calculated as 10,000 + n (Actual value)

title.narrative: Number of women-led business supported with registration of their businesses

comment.narrative: The project is financing several women lead enterprises and is in the process of identifying those who need help formalizing and registering. This process is underway and the first results are expected in mid-2026.

title.narrative: Forest area brought under management plans

comment.narrative: 44 forest management plans covering 340,958 hectares of land are awaiting approval, expected in the first quarter of 2026. Once approved, the indicator will be updated.

title.narrative: Target beneficiaries with rating “Satisfied” with project interventions (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: A satisfaction survey will be carried out among beneficiaries in the first half of 2026, by which 75% of sub-project work is expected to be completed. The indicator will be updated when results are available, around the end of 2026.

title.narrative: Forest area managed by local community groups using sustainable forest management practices

comment.narrative: Areas developed under the FACI model, managed by community groups, will be counted towards the indicator by June 2026.

Deployment of the MRV (Measurement, Reporting and Verification) system began in January 2025, with a completion date of 12 months. The first assessments of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are expected in the first half of 2026 which will allow for the indicator to be updated.

title.narrative: Pastoral zones brought under management plans

comment.narrative: Five pastoral unit management plans and ten pastoral area development plans will be implemented during 2026. The indicator is expected to be updated in the first half of 2026.

title.narrative: People with increased access to income earning opportunities (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: The sub-components related to this indicator will be implemented in the second quarter of 2025. Results are expected at the beginning of 2026 and the indicator will be updated accordingly.

title.narrative: Area of pastures rehabilitated through climate adaptation strategies

comment.narrative: This indicator is linked to the implementation of related sub-projects and the pasture management plans, which has been delayed. The sub-projects associated with bourgouculture and forage perimeters will impact 502 ha and 919 ha respectively. The creation of five pastoral units will help restore 1,800 hectares of grazing land. All in all, 3,221 ha of grazing land are expected to be rehabilitated by December 2025. The indicator will be updated in mid-June 2026.

title.narrative: Restored areas in Niger Inner Delta (different types of activities)

comment.narrative: To date, 11 sub projects have been completed out of the 53 areas under restoration. These 53 areas are comprised of 04 investment projects, 48 landscape restoration projects and 01 Forest Management Plans. The annual target has been exceeded.
118 management agreements have been signed within the framework of the sub-projects. The target has been exceeded.

title.narrative: Area of non-forested land under agroforestry/afforestation

comment.narrative: The annual target has been exceeded. There are 42 agroforestry sub-projects covering an area of 1,182 ha after field measurement.

title.narrative: Area restored/developed through opening of water channels to mitigate the impact of climate-induced floods

comment.narrative: 4 Niger Inner Delta projects which will contribute to restoration/development of areas floods are underway. These projects should be completed in by the end of 2026.

title.narrative: Percentage of women-led associations receiving financial grants and technical support

comment.narrative: Among the associations being supported, 28% are led by women.

title.narrative: Restored landscapes crossed by the GGWI belt in Mali

comment.narrative: To date, of the 73 projects in the GGW in progress, 4 have been completed. The 73 projects are comprised of 70 landscape restoration sub-projects and 3 projects to implement management plans for gazetted forests. The completion of several more sub-projects is anticipated in early to mid 2026, which will allow for the indicator to be updated.

title.narrative: Business plans supported by the project (NTFPs and fisheries products)

comment.narrative: The annual target has been exceeded. Twenty-five business plans relating to NTFPs and 40 relating to fishery products have been selected for support, with 58 already beginning activities.

title.narrative: Certificate / diploma delivered through capacity development trainings (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: 150 managers were trained in 2024. In 2025, 592 people were trained, including 81 women for a total of 742 people trained, of which 104 are women (14%).
A total of 87 Economic, Social and Cultural Development Plans (PDESC) have been adopted by communal councils. The project target has been met.

title.narrative: Land area under sustainable landscape management practices

comment.narrative:
To date, 14,738 hectares are under SLM through the implementation of 118 sub-projects. With the planned second batch of SLM sub-projects together with the NTFP sub-projects, number of hectares are projected to increase by more than 200,000 ha by the end of 2026.
The value for the period is calculated as 10,000 + n (Actual value)

Six (06) sites selected as part of the FACI development works, covering a total area of 1,460 hectares. These sites are in the pre-project study phase. This indicator will be updated to reflect progress starting June 2026 after implementation begins.

title.narrative: Mali MRV and National forest information system (SIFOR) operational

comment.narrative: The technical note for the MRV has been validated and equipment purchased. The project will proceed with setting up the technical, digital components of the system.
